discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands and correlated and superconducting phases in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: moiré quantum materials
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic' angle near 1.1 degrees would make the Dirac bands nearly flat, so that interactions would dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group confirmed this dramatically: magic-angle bilayer graphene showed correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity that could be tuned with a gate voltage. The work founded twistronics. The twist angle is now a new control knob for quantum matter, and moiré systems have produced orbital ferromagnetism, quantized anomalous Hall states, and fractional Chern insulators at zero magnetic field. The discovery joins symmetry, topology and strong correlations in one clean, tunable platform. It has changed what both experimentalists and theorists look for, much as high-Tc cuprates once did. This is theory telling experiment exactly what to build, followed by an experiment that opened a whole new class of materials.
